tool.name: OGSTools yaml2vtu
tool.description: Mesh a geometric model from a YAML file and convert it to VTU
tool.help:
**Overview**
`yaml2vtu` builds a two-dimensional mesh from a geometric model described in a YAML file. The geometry is created with Gmsh, and the resulting mesh is then converted to VTU meshes with the same conversion `msh2vtu` performs: one dataset for the bulk mesh (`domain`) and one for each physical group defined in the geometry file.
The YAML file has four required blocks, plus an optional `parameters` block:
```yaml parameters: # optional, available by name in expressions tunnel_radius: 6.0
points: # name: coordinates and target element size center: { coords: [0.0, 0.0], char_length: 0.3 }
lines: # start/end point names, optionally an arc tunnel_arc_top: { start: top_tunnel, end: bottom_tunnel, center: center }
surfaces: # closed curve loops bounding a surface tunnel: loops: - [tunnel_arc_top, tunnel_arc_bottom] - ["-tunnel_arc_bottom", "-tunnel_arc_top"] # -name reverses a line
groups: # physical groups, become the output meshes BoundaryTunnel: dim: 1 entities: [tunnel_arc_top, tunnel_arc_bottom] Domain: dim: 2 entities: [tunnel] ```
Coordinates, target element sizes and parameter values may be written as expressions that refer to the `parameters` block and to the functions of the `math` module, e.g. `"tunnel_radius + wall_thickness"`.
**Inputs**
- **Geometry definition**: the YAML file describing the geometry.
**Outputs**
A collection of VTU meshes: `domain` holds the bulk mesh, one further dataset is created per physical group, named after that group (e.g. `Domain`, `BoundaryTunnel`).
